FR-001.line: - **FR-001**: The tool MUST accept Markdown table content from standard input.

FR-002.line: - **FR-002**: The tool MUST accept Markdown table content from a file path provided by the user.

FR-003.line: - **FR-003**: The tool MUST convert each Markdown table row into a corresponding CSV row.

FR-004.line: - **FR-004**: The tool MUST preserve the order of columns and rows from the source table.

FR-005.line: - **FR-005**: The tool MUST preserve header rows when they are present in the Markdown input.

FR-006.line: - **FR-006**: The tool MUST produce CSV-compliant escaping for commas, quotes, and line breaks inside cell values.

FR-007.line: - **FR-007**: The tool MUST treat empty table cells as empty CSV fields.

FR-008.line: - **FR-008**: The tool MUST ignore Markdown formatting characters that are not part of the cell content.

FR-009.line: - **FR-009**: The tool MUST report a clear message when no valid Markdown table is found in the input.

FR-010.line: - **FR-010**: The tool MUST report a clear message when the input cannot be read or parsed as a table.

SC-001.line: - **SC-001**: Users can convert a valid Markdown table to CSV in a single command with no manual cleanup for at least 95% of typical documentation tables.

SC-002.line: - **SC-002**: At least 90% of first-time users can successfully convert a sample table without consulting additional instructions.

SC-003.line: - **SC-003**: For valid input, the tool preserves all table rows and columns exactly as presented in the source table structure.

SC-004.line: - **SC-004**: When the input contains no valid table, users receive a clear error message in all tested cases.
